senses: Any large herbivorous ungulate mammal native to Africa and Asia of the family Rhinocerotidae, with thick, gray skin and one or two horns on their snouts.
ety: From Latin rhīnocerōs, from Ancient Greek ῥῑνόκερως (rhīnókerōs, “nose-horned”), composed of ῥῑ́ς, ῥῑνός (rhī́s, rhīnós, “nose, of (the) nose”) + κέρας (kéras, “horn”).

senses: A principal low-level cloud type, predominantly stratiform, in the form of a gray and/or whitish layer or patch, which nearly always has dark parts and is nonfibrous.
ety: From strato- + cumulus.

senses: One who, or that which, twitters.
ety: From twitter + -er.

senses: A psychological disorder in which a person has a delusion of a romantic relationship with another person.
Excessive sexual inclination or desire.
ety: From late 19th century. From Ancient Greek ἐρωτικός (erōtikós, “related to love”), which is from ἔρως (érōs, “passionate or sexual love”); eroto- + -mania.

senses: A mace bearer; specifically, an officer of a court in Scotland.
ety: From Middle English macer, from Anglo-Norman macer, from mace (“mace”).

senses: An usher to a riding master (riding instructor).
ety: French, ultimately from Latin creatus (“created, begotten”); compare Italian creato (“pupil, servant”), Spanish criado (“a servant, client”).

senses: A sheaf of wheat, or its representation used as an emblem.
ety: From wheat + sheaf.

senses: Somewhat blond in colour.
Similar to a stereotypical dumb blonde.
ety: From blond + -ish.
examples: I had a blondish moment earlier: I accidentally locked my keys inside my hotel room.

senses: The hairstyle and characteristic bald patch resulting from being tonsured.
A ritual shaving of this kind.
ety: From Middle English tonsure, from Anglo-Norman and Old French tonsure, from Latin tonsūra (“a clipping, trimming”), from tondeō (“shear, clip, trim”).

senses: A polymer, polyethylene terephthalate PET, as used for making thread and cloth.
ety: Originated in 1951 (as Dacron) as a trademark, modern coinage by E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co. on the model of nylon.

senses: Covered with heather.
Having flecks produced by interwoven yarns of mixed colours.
ety: From heather + -ed.

senses: A hard, straw-colored cow's-milk cheese with a nutty flavor.
ety: Named for the Appenzell region of Switzerland

senses: To make (someone or something) sensitive or responsive to certain stimuli.
To make (someone) increasingly aware of, in a concerned or sensitive way.
To render capable of being acted on by actinic rays of light.
ety: From sensitive + -ize.
examples: Anaphylaxis is the syndrome elicited in a hypersensitive subject upon subsequent exposure to the sensitizing antigen.
Again, I strongly recommend that you sensitize your collodion-coated plates in a tank, rather than a tray, as it is safer, cleaner, and more process-efficient.
Ever since the burglary, we've been more sensitized to home security issues.

senses: To move in a messy, liquid manner.
To smush, to smash.
ety: Imitative? The sense "gush" (at least) is related to gush. The sense "smush" may be related to smoosh.
examples: The ground gooshed in places, soggy from the winter rains.
I waded out, my hair streaming water down my back, my toes gooshing deliciously in the mud.

Risu looked for the bees but they were nowhere to be found—not even a gooshed one, and surely she must've gooshed at least a few during her frantic swatting. Pesky things. A movement to the left attracted her eye.

senses: The act of counting or numbering; enumeration.
Any system of giving names to numbers.
ety: From Middle English numeracioun, from Latin numerātiō. By surface analysis, numerate + -ion.

senses: Furnished with a bastion; having bastions.
ety: From bastion + -ed.
examples: To the North there were low pale-colored hills, in places bastioned with rock.

senses: Resembling a leaf or leaves.
Bearing leaves.
ety: From Latin foliaceus, from folium (“a leaf”).
examples: I have one specimen, in which the primary crystals are siliceous, the secondary thin foliaceous crystals of deep red but transparent iron-ore, forming elegant figures, that have the form of roses.

The bitter principle contained in the root, wood and bark was discovered by Blunse who named it samaderin; it is a white, crystalline, foliaceous substance, more soluble in water than in alcohol, fusible.

senses: The belief in, participation in, or sanction of destroying religious icons and other symbols or monuments, usually with religious or political motives.
A challenge to a widely held belief, tradition or cherished institution.
ety: From iconoclast.

senses: A soft French cow's-milk cheese from the Alpine region of Savoie.
ety: Borrowed from French, from reblocher (“to pinch a cow's udder again”).

senses: A wiener sausage.
ety: From wien(er) + -ie.

senses: A person who makes malt; a maltster.
ety: From Middle English maltare, malter, maltar; equivalent to malt + -er.

senses: Characterized by scurf; covered with scurf.
ety: From scurf + -y.

senses: One whose beliefs accord with womanism.
ety: From woman + -ist. Late 20th c., after humanist.

senses: A position in which the feet are apart, or a movement which brings them apart.
An open-crotch undergarment.
ety: Borrowed from French ouvert. Doublet of apert and overt.

senses: Exhibiting strong, masculine beauty.
Shaped like a hunk, or piece; chunky.
ety: From hunk + -y.

senses: The layer of the Earth's atmosphere directly above the mesosphere and directly below the exosphere.
ety: From thermo- + -sphere.

senses: The range of a melody, especially those of ecclesiastical chants.
A canvassing for votes.
ety: From Latin ambitus (“circuit, ostentation”). Doublet of ambit.

senses: A pious observance such as fasting and pilgrimage.
ety: Transliteration of Sanskrit व्रत (vratá). Related to the group word, verb, and verve, from the same Proto-Indo-European root, *werh₁- (“to speak, say”).

senses: A virus which causes this infection (Orthpoxvirus vaccinia).
A closely related poxvirus, used as a smallpox vaccine.
ety: From Latin vaccinus + -ia.

senses: An ideology according to which a nation is an organic unit, transcending conflict between social and economic groups.
A movement within Roman Catholicism, holding that political rule must not be separated from religious issues.
ety: From integral + -ism.

senses: Arsenic trisulphide, occurring naturally in crystals or massive deposits, formerly used as a dye or pigment.
ety: From Middle English orpyment, from Old French orpiment, from Latin auripigmentum (“orpiment”), from aurum (“gold”) + pigmentum (“pigment”).

senses: Transsexuality; the state of being transsexual.
ety: From transsexual + -ism.
examples: Transfolk are not covered in any applicable laws like Title VII or the ADA - in fact, transsexualism is explicitly excluded from the ADA. Therefore, you have no causes of action against an employer based on federal law.

senses: Capable of being set.
ety: From set + -able.

senses: An extrovert.
ety: From out + -ie.

senses: The study of human action or conduct.
ety: From Ancient Greek πρᾶξις (prâxis) + -logy.

senses: One who plays a musical instrument, as distinguished from a vocalist.
An adherent of instrumentalism.
ety: From instrumental + -ist.

senses: A specific, widely-planted variety of red wine grape, or a wine made from such grapes.
ety: From French grenache, from Italian vernaccia, from Vernazza, a town in Italy. Cognate to Catalan garnatxa, Spanish garnacha, Portuguese garnacha.

senses: A plane-like tool used by coopers for smoothing and chamfering their work, especially the inside of casks.
ety: From the same source as German Hobel. Related to Danish høvl and Swedish hyvel.

senses: Covered with brick.
Similar to brick in texture, colour, shape, etc.
ety: From brick + -y.

senses: Any of a number of Central American and South American freshwater fish in the family Cichlidae.
ety: Borrowed from Brazilian Portuguese acará, borrowed from Old Tupi akará, from Proto-Tupi-Guarani *akara.
